A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Closed-Form Diffusion Models by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-distribution, surface-sampling, Butterflies and CelebA experiments, including sample-quality metrics, runtimes and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original noise, step-size, latent-space and neural-model analyses in Appendices D–H.

M1.justification: Score smoothing, Algorithm 1, late-start sampling and the nearest-neighbor score estimator are unchanged. The added experiments vary existing parameters or evaluate comparison models without introducing a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds Two Spirals, a 100-dimensional Gaussian distribution and MNIST to the retained coverage. These support new evaluations of neural-field approximation, finite-step memorization and image-denoising behavior in Appendices G–H.

E2.justification: Appendix H newly evaluates neural flow-matching models against CFDM behavior: a three-layer MLP on 2D datasets and a UNet on MNIST. The existing Butterflies DDPM and CelebA VAE comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include moment-matched Gaussian/Gumbel smoothing, noisy-velocity controls, a 1–100-step sweep, velocity-field squared-error measurements and convex-hull regression. The MNIST analysis trains on 60,000 images and evaluates 512 test images. Existing Appendix C protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 already examines sigma, start time, nearest-neighbor approximation and M on synthetic data. v3 extends the M ablation to CelebA and adds smoothing-noise robustness, integration-noise and step-size controls, plus detailed comparisons of CFDM and neural-model behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions report plus/minus values for inception score and KID. New Tables 3–4 continue this practice without adding seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence-interval definitions or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their values. New Tables 3–4 report latent-space ablation results, including Gaussian/Gumbel KIDs of 0.091±0.0071 and 0.092±0.0082. Figure 14 adds 88.8% and 81.1% reductions in neural-field approximation error on Checkerboard and Spirals. Further new results document memorization and MNIST behavior.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 replaces the bounded-distance Lipschitz argument with a covariance-Jacobian bound based on dataset diameter. Proposition B.3 changes from O(1/epsilon²) amplification to an exponential-dependent factor, while the fixed-T, fixed-epsilon O(sigma) statement remains. Appendices F–G add mathematical arguments about sampling noise and finite step sizes.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions are unchanged. Both versions claim training-free generalization through smoothing, barycentric sample support, nearest-neighbor acceleration and practical CPU sampling.

C2.justification: v3 substantially develops the relationship to neural generalization: approximation deteriorates near the terminal time, and MNIST neural denoisers can point outside the training-data convex hull. It extends the interpretation of large-M concentration to latent faces and makes the image-quality gap and applicability limits more explicit in the conclusion.

D1.justification: Appendix H supplies architecture, activation, optimizer, learning-rate and epoch details for the new neural experiments, along with MNIST sampling and projected-gradient regression procedures. Existing implementation and data-access information in Appendix C is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Aithal et al. (2024) on diffusion hallucinations arising from smooth score approximations. Appendix H connects its findings to the already-cited Kamb and Ganguli work. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained. Local additions clarify tuple indexing and sigma selection, expand the conclusion, and add publication information and acknowledgements. The new scientific analyses appear in additional appendix sections without extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3–4 and Figures 10–18, including latent-image grids, memorization plots, neural velocity-field comparisons and MNIST denoising panels. Existing figures are retained with layout changes, including relocation of Figure 4 and the original appendix Figures 8–9.

improvement.justification: The added controls and neural-model diagnostics strengthen evidence for the generalization mechanism and clarify its limits. Appendix B.3 also restores v2's missing exponential in error propagation. However, revised Equation 13 implies beta(T)<1 for 0<T<1/2 and positive dataset diameter, contradicting beta(T)=1 from its definition. The stronger empirical support provides a net improvement, but the unresolved theoretical defect limits the quality gain.
